otherDetail: Other income was a net $6M expense: $17M of other income, net, less $22M of interest expense. A separate $8M share of loss from an equity investee, net of taxes, is shown as equityM (amounts rounded from thousands). Stock-based compensation was $84M in the quarter, $7M of it in cost of sales; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.41 versus GAAP $0.31.

segments.name: Total net sales
segments.note: Supermicro reports a single operating segment and printed no product split for the quarter. Sales are mostly complete server and rack systems: for the full fiscal year, server and storage systems were 97.0% of net sales and subsystems and accessories 3.0% (10-K), and services and software were $330.5M. Four customers each accounted for 10% or more of FY25 net sales.

sources.label: Form 10-K for the year ended Jun 30, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Net sales hit $5,757M, up from $5,355M a year ago, yet net income fell 34% to $195M from $297M. Gross margin narrowed to 9.5% from 10.2% and operating costs rose 23%, so the extra sales did not reach the bottom line.
takeaways.title: Sales grew, but profit shrank by a third

takeaways.text: Cost of sales ate $5,213M of the $5,757M in sales, leaving a 9.5% gross margin — down from 10.2% a year ago and 9.6% last quarter. Operating income fell 21% to $228M as R&D jumped 44% YoY to $183M on hiring for next-generation server and rack designs.
takeaways.title: Thin margins are the story

takeaways.text: Operations generated $864M of cash in the quarter, against $79M of capital expenditures and investments. Cash ended June 30 at $5.2B versus $4.8B of bank debt and convertible notes. For the full year, sales grew 47% to $22.0B while net income fell to $1.0B from $1.2B.
takeaways.title: Cash came back strongly

verdict: Supermicro's sales rose 7.5% to $5.8B, but thinner margins and higher R&D spending cut profit by a third to $195M — even as the quarter generated $864M of operating cash.
